attempts.summary: Implemented an Ansible-driven VRRP failover gateway so node3 reaches node4 through a single, always-available next hop that prefers node1. Topology: node1/node2 (VyOS) bridge two private L2 segments - network A (10.20.1.0/24: node1-eth1, node2-eth1, node3-enp8s0) and network B (10.20.2.0/24: node1-eth2, node2-eth2, node4-enp8s0). Two VRRP groups (NET_A vrid21 on eth1, NET_B vrid22 on eth2), bundled in a sync-group so they fail over together, provide a stable VIP on each segment (10.20.1.1 / 10.20.2.1); node1 has priority 200 (preferred MASTER), node2 has priority 100 (BACKUP, preempts back once node1 recovers). node3 has a static route to 10.20.2.0/24 via 10.20.1.1 (its single gateway for reaching node4); node4 has the symmetric route back via 10.20.2.1. All configuration is applied by an idempotent Ansible playbook run from node5 (the designated control node, which has ansible-core) against inventory groups 'routers' (node1/node2, via SSH+sudo raw VyOS configure/set/commit/save) and 'endpoints' (node3/node4, via nmcli static NetworkManager profiles). Verified live failover by rebooting node1 while continuously pinging node3->node4: zero packet loss, node2 promoted to MASTER within seconds; node1 rejoined and preempted back to MASTER after its reboot completed. Completed the mandatory per-node restart-evidence protocol for all 5 nodes one at a time (boot_id captured before/after and confirmed changed, services/config/connectivity verified recovered each time, quorum/master preserved throughout), and re-ran the Ansible playbook afterward confirming full idempotency and persistence across reboots.
